--- title: "[chunk.RetrievedChunk]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-dataclass}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} A chunk returned from a retrieval operation with associated metrics. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/docs-embedding-providers/src/raghilda/chunk.py#L179-L228){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python chunk.RetrievedChunk( text, start_index, end_index, char_count, context=None, origin=None, attributes=None, metrics=list(), chunk_ids=list() ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `store.retrieve()` returns `RetrievedChunk` objects rather than plain `Chunk`s. Each one is an ordinary `Chunk` (text, position, context, origin, attributes) extended with the scores that explain *why* it was returned, so you can rank, threshold, or display results and still trace each passage back to its source. In addition to the inherited `Chunk` fields, `RetrievedChunk` adds: ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [metrics]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Metric]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [list()
]{.doc-parameter-default} : Retrieval scores for this chunk, as a list of `Metric` objects. With the default hybrid retrieval a chunk may carry several (for example a vector similarity score and a BM25 score); higher values indicate a better match. [chunk_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [list()
]{.doc-parameter-default} : Backend chunk identifiers represented by this retrieved chunk. A normal result contains a single id; a deoverlapped result that merged several adjacent chunks lists all of their ids. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Construct one directly to see its shape (in practice `store.retrieve()` builds these for you). Here we attach two scores and then read them back: ::: {#9fa083e9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from raghilda.chunk import RetrievedChunk, Metric chunk = RetrievedChunk( text="This is relevant content.", start_index=0, end_index=25, char_count=25, metrics=[ Metric(name="similarity", value=0.92), Metric(name="bm25_score", value=15.3), ], ) # Each Metric carries a name and a numeric score for metric in chunk.metrics: print(f"{metric.name}: {metric.value}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` similarity: 0.92 bm25_score: 15.3 ``` ::: :::
